test_stimuli.name: ch0_mid_scale
test_stimuli.derivation: high_byte=0x7F, low_byte=0xFF; raw = ((0x7F & 0x03) << 8) | 0xFF = (0x03 << 8) | 0xFF = 0x3FF = 1023; but 10-bit max is 1023, so 511 is mid-scale? Wait: 0x7F & 0x03 = 0x03, (0x03 << 8) = 0x300, | 0xFF = 0x3FF = 1023. That's full scale. high_byte bits[1:0]=0x01, low_byte=0xFF. So stream bytes: dummy=0x00, high_byte=0x7F? Actually high_byte = (raw >> 8) & 0x03 = 0x01, so byte1 = 0x40? Wait: The response bytes: byte0=dummy, byte1[1:0]=ADC[9:8], byte2=ADC[7:0]. For raw=511 (0x1FF): ADC[9:8]=0x01, ADC[7:0]=0xFF. So byte1 = 0x40? No, byte1[1:0] = 0x01, so byte1 = 0x01? Actually the byte1 is the second byte returned; its top 6 bits are don't care, bottom 2 bits are ADC[9:8]. So byte1 = 0x01. byte2 = 0xFF. So stream = [0x00, 0x01, 0xFF]. But we need to ensure the driver reads 3 bytes. So mock_preload stream = [0x00, 0x01, 0xFF]. Then expected_channels ch0 = ((0x01 & 0x03) << 8) | 0xFF = (1 << 8) | 255 = 256 + 255 = 511.
